name: Approximate device RAM
plain: RAM in gigabytes, rounded down to a power of two and capped at 8.
meaning: Lets a site serve a light page to low-memory phones. Rounded to 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 or 8 GB, so a 32 GB workstation and an 8 GB laptop look identical.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: deviceMemory
fields.precision: rounded down to power of two, max 8

limits.headline: Can see roughly how much RAM you have, rounded and capped at 8 GB
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads in Chrome or Edge
can: Send a lighter page to low memory phones
Use the number as one hardware clue
cannot: See your exact RAM; a 32 GB machine looks like 8
Work in Firefox, Safari, or on iPhone
See how much memory is free right now
Work on pages that are not HTTPS
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, and Samsung Internet share it. Firefox and Safari share nothing.

story.what_it_is: Tells a page roughly how much memory your device has, capped at 8 GB.

marketing.name: Navigator.deviceMemory
marketing.pitch: Documents a rough, rounded memory figure that lets pages adapt to low-end devices.

story.for_you: You never see it asked. If your phone has little memory, a site may quietly give you a lighter version so it does not crash. If you have a big machine, you get the full version.
story.for_makers: Sites use it to serve light pages to low-memory phones and heavy pages to strong machines. It is capped and rounded, so a 32 GB workstation looks like 8 GB. It still adds a clue to a fingerprint.

use_cases.example: A shop serves smaller images and fewer scripts to a phone that reports 2 GB, so the page loads fast.
A browser game turns down textures and crowd count on devices that report 2 GB or less.
A video site loads fewer thumbnails ahead of time on a low-memory phone.
A browser editor warns that a large file may crash on a device with little memory.
A news site drops heavy interactive graphics for low-memory visitors.
An ad network picks lighter ad formats for low-memory phones to avoid freezing the page.
A fraud tool treats an impossible combination of memory and device model as a sign of a fake.
